content: The above PR just renames a few declarations, but causes the tests for the continuity tactic to fail. I don't see why this would happen (all renamed declarations are tagged continuity both before and after the change). Does anybody know why and would like to help me fix or diagnose this?

Yeah that is pretty weird! 

example {f : X → Y} (x : X) : Continuous (fun (_ : X) ↦ f x) := by continuity

now fails (line 28 of MathlibTest/Continuity.lean). continuity is supposed to be just aesop with a prescribed ruleset. On master the proof unfolds to exact continuous_const, which has been renamed Continuous.const in this PR. Weirdly, the aesop error in the PR is

tactic 'aesop' failed, failed to prove the goal after exhaustive search.
Initial goal:

W : Type ?u.43426
X : Type u_1
Y : Type u_2
Z : Type ?u.43435
inst✝⁴ : TopologicalSpace W
inst✝³ : TopologicalSpace X
inst✝² : TopologicalSpace Y
inst✝¹ : TopologicalSpace Z
I : Type ?u.43438
X' : I → Type ?u.43443
inst✝ : (i : I) → TopologicalSpace (X' i)
f : X → Y
x : X
⊢ Continuous fun x_1 => f x

Remaining goals after safe rules:

case hg
W : Type ?u.43426
X : Type u_1
Y : Type u_2
Z : Type ?u.43435
inst : TopologicalSpace W
inst_1 : TopologicalSpace X
inst_2 : TopologicalSpace Y
inst_3 : TopologicalSpace Z
I : Type ?u.43438
X' : I → Type ?u.43443
inst_4 : (i : I) → TopologicalSpace (X' i)
f : X → Y
x : X
⊢ Continuous f

so something has gone wrong here -- aesop has applied a rule which isn't safe in its "safe" rules, because Continuous f is not provable whereas the goal (continuity of the constant function sending anything in X to f x) is certainly true.

Conjecture: (a) the renaming in the PR changes the order in which aesop applies things, and (b) continuity is assuming that certain applications are "safe", for example "if the goal is to prove that f \circ g is continuous, and we know already that g is continuous, then it's safe to reduce the goal to the claim that f is continuous". So (a) is exposing some kind of non-confluence and the usually-safe (b) is tripping us up because another reason that f \circ g can be continuous is that g is constant and f is arbitrary -- something which was tried first in master and is being tried too late in this PR.
Tangential questions: do we have any tests where fun_prop still fails but continuity succeeds?
We do have a few places in mathlib where fun_prop fails and continuity or simpa using by fun_prop would work. I'm not sure if we have tests for this.

Thanks a lot for the guesswork, this was really helpful. I think your theory is spot-on --- docs#Continuous.comp' is tagged with continuity, which internally is a safe aesop rule. Making it an unsafe rule fixes these failures.

Making that change causes two other tests to break though --- including one where aesop behaves in non-intuitive ways:

  • when tagging Continuous.comp' as safe, it succeeds quickly,
  • when tagging it as unsafe, it always fails (even with 95% or 99% success probability)
  • increasing the maximum rule application depth makes simp time out, so is also not a solution

@Jannis Limperg Do you know why this is? #36806 is a self-contained PR which should reproduce this problem.
At this point, this bug is taking up much more of my time than it's worth, so it's tempting to comment the test cases with a note about this and move on.
Cross-referencing #mathlib4 > aesop error during proof reconstruction, goal not normalised, for a different aesop bug found during minimisation.
